description: 45 healthcare logos explained by a brand designer, from Mayo Clinic and Cleveland Clinic to Pfizer, CVS Health, Oscar, and Hims & Hers.
intro:
A healthcare logo has a harder job than most: it has to feel trustworthy enough for a hospital bed and friendly enough for an app on your phone, often at the same time.

What makes a good healthcare logo?

Trust first: patients meet these logos on hospital signs, insurance cards, and prescription bottles, so clarity and stability matter more than novelty.

Symbols with meaning: the best marks, like the Mayo Clinic shields or the Cleveland Clinic cross, carry a real story instead of a generic heart or stethoscope.

Color that calms: blues and greens dominate the category, which is exactly why brands like Mount Sinai, CVS Health, and Headspace stand out with pink, red, and orange.

Below are 45 healthcare logos in five groups, from hospitals and insurers to pharma, medtech, and digital health. Each one has a slide with my handwritten notes, followed by a short explanation.

logoResearch.name: Mayo Clinic
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Mayo Clinic is a nonprofit academic medical center founded in Rochester, Minnesota.
observations: Three interlocking shields stand for patient care, research, and education, the three parts of Mayo's mission.
The stacked, all-caps wordmark is set in a calm, institutional sans that lets the shields lead.

logoResearch.name: Cleveland Clinic
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Cleveland Clinic is a nonprofit academic medical center headquartered in Cleveland, Ohio.
observations: Four green squares frame a white cross, a medical symbol built from simple geometry rather than an illustration.
The two-word wordmark in grey sans keeps the green symbol as the only accent.

logoResearch.name: Johns Hopkins Medicine
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Johns Hopkins Medicine unites the Johns Hopkins University School of Medicine and the Johns Hopkins Health System in Baltimore.
observations: The shield shows the hospital's famous dome, tying the brand to its historic Baltimore building.
A condensed serif and a widely spaced MEDICINE line give the lockup an academic, established feel.

logoResearch.name: Kaiser Permanente
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Kaiser Permanente is an integrated health care organization that combines health plans, hospitals, and medical groups.
observations: The symbol is a rising sun made of people-like rays, a hopeful image of health and community.
Spaced, all-caps letters in one blue keep the long name readable and calm.

logoResearch.name: Mass General Brigham
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Mass General Brigham is a Boston health system formed by Massachusetts General Hospital and Brigham and Women's Hospital.
observations: The columns symbol suggests a classical hospital building and the history of both founding hospitals.
A friendly blue sans balances the classical columns with a modern, approachable tone.

logoResearch.name: NYU Langone Health
logoResearch.verifiedFact: NYU Langone Health is the academic medical center of New York University.
observations: An open, sweeping arc wraps the name, suggesting care that surrounds the patient.
NYU's violet connects the medical center to the university brand.

logoResearch.name: Mount Sinai
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Mount Sinai Health System is a New York City health system anchored by The Mount Sinai Hospital.
observations: Overlapping colored lines form a mountain peak, a direct, modern take on the name.
The bright gradient of pink, blue, and violet stands out in a category full of navy logos.

logoResearch.name: Providence
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Providence is a not-for-profit health system founded by the Sisters of Providence.
observations: The cross is built from four colored segments, nodding to the system's Catholic roots.
A classic serif wordmark adds warmth and tradition.

logoResearch.name: HCA Healthcare
logoResearch.verifiedFact: HCA Healthcare is one of the largest hospital operators in the United States.
observations: A heavy HCA acronym is paired with an orange plus sign that reads as medical care at a glance.
The second line in a softer serif makes the acronym feel less corporate.

logoResearch.name: UnitedHealth Group
logoResearch.verifiedFact: UnitedHealth Group is a health care company that includes the insurer UnitedHealthcare and the services business Optum.
observations: The logo is a pure wordmark, with no symbol, set in wide, spaced capitals.
Navy blue and generous letterspacing signal stability, the main job of an insurer's brand.

logoResearch.name: Aetna
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Aetna is a US health insurer that is part of CVS Health.
observations: A violet heart sits next to the name, connecting the insurer to its CVS Health parent.
The rounded, bold lowercase wordmark makes insurance feel friendly.

logoResearch.name: Cigna Healthcare
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Cigna Healthcare is the health benefits business of The Cigna Group.
observations: The tree of life symbol is made of small green and blue leaves, suggesting growth and well-being.
A rounded lowercase wordmark sits directly under the tree.

logoResearch.name: Humana
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Humana is a US health insurer focused on Medicare Advantage plans.
observations: Humana uses a green wordmark with no symbol, so the color does all the work.
The soft, rounded letters make the name feel human, a nod to the brand name itself.

logoResearch.name: Elevance Health
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Elevance Health, formerly Anthem, is a US health insurer that runs Anthem Blue Cross Blue Shield plans.
observations: A small chevron above the E points upward, illustrating the idea of elevating health.
Two weights of navy type separate the name from the descriptor.

logoResearch.name: Blue Cross Blue Shield
logoResearch.verifiedFact: The Blue Cross Blue Shield Association is a federation of independent health insurance companies in the US.
observations: Two separate symbols, a cross and a shield, reflect the two organizations the brand grew from.
The symbols are shared by dozens of local companies, so they work as a mark of trust more than a single company logo.

logoResearch.name: Oscar Health
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Oscar Health is a technology-focused US health insurer founded in 2012.
observations: A bright blue, geometric lowercase wordmark looks more like a consumer app than an insurer.
The perfectly round letters make the brand friendly and simple, the opposite of traditional insurance.

logoResearch.name: Molina Healthcare
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Molina Healthcare is a US health insurer focused on Medicaid and Medicare plans.
observations: Three teal figures, two adults and a child, show a family, the people the plans serve.
A stacked wordmark in two weights separates MOLINA from HEALTHCARE.

logoResearch.name: Centene
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Centene is a large US managed care company that serves government-sponsored health plans.
observations: A bold, condensed blue wordmark reads as strong and corporate.
The light grey Corporation line underneath adds a formal, institutional tone.

logoResearch.name: Pfizer
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Pfizer is a global pharmaceutical company based in New York.
observations: The 2021 symbol is a double helix that also echoes Pfizer's historic pill shape.
An italic script wordmark gives the brand forward motion and a human touch.

logoResearch.name: Johnson & Johnson
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Johnson & Johnson is a global health care company focused on pharmaceuticals and medical technology.
observations: In 2023 the company replaced its famous script with a clean, modern sans wordmark.
The signature red stayed, so the new logo still feels like J&J.

logoResearch.name: Novartis
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Novartis is a Swiss pharmaceutical company based in Basel.
observations: The symbol is an abstract flame in blue, orange, and yellow, suggesting energy and progress.
A wide, classic serif wordmark in spaced capitals keeps the brand serious and scientific.

logoResearch.name: AstraZeneca
logoResearch.verifiedFact: AstraZeneca is a British-Swedish pharmaceutical company.
observations: The gold symbol suggests a twisting molecule or a figure in motion.
A plum wordmark with a capital Z joins two company names into one.

logoResearch.name: Moderna
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Moderna is a US biotechnology company known for its mRNA medicines and vaccines.
observations: A thin, red lowercase wordmark feels light and modern, like a tech company.
The dotted line underneath suggests a strand of genetic code.

logoResearch.name: Sanofi
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Sanofi is a French pharmaceutical company based in Paris.
observations: The 2022 rebrand replaced a colorful bird symbol with a simple black lowercase wordmark.
Two purple dots built into the s are the logo's only color.

logoResearch.name: GSK
logoResearch.verifiedFact: GSK is a British pharmaceutical company, formerly GlaxoSmithKline.
observations: The 2022 rebrand shortened the name to three letters and made them the whole logo.
An orange gradient keeps the brand's heritage color but feels more energetic.

logoResearch.name: Novo Nordisk
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Novo Nordisk is a Danish pharmaceutical company known for diabetes and obesity medicines.
observations: The Apis bull, an ancient Egyptian symbol, is one of the oldest marks in pharma.
A clean lowercase novo sits next to the bull in deep blue.

logoResearch.name: Lilly
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Eli Lilly and Company is a US pharmaceutical company based in Indianapolis.
observations: The red script logo is based on the signature of founder Colonel Eli Lilly.
The long swash under the letters makes the wordmark instantly recognizable.

logoResearch.name: CVS Health
logoResearch.verifiedFact: CVS Health is a US health company that runs CVS Pharmacy, Aetna, and other businesses.
observations: The red heart was added in 2014, when CVS stopped selling tobacco.
A bold CVS and a lighter Health split the name into brand and category.

logoResearch.name: Walgreens
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Walgreens is one of the largest pharmacy chains in the United States.
observations: The red script wordmark dates back decades and is one of the most recognizable in retail.
The flowing W connects the letters into one continuous signature.

logoResearch.name: Medtronic
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Medtronic is one of the world's largest medical device companies.
observations: Medtronic uses a strong navy wordmark with no symbol.
Tight spacing and heavy letters make the name feel solid and technical.

logoResearch.name: Stryker
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Stryker is a US medical technology company known for orthopedic and surgical products.
observations: A heavy, rounded black wordmark has the look of strong industrial equipment.
The low, wide letters feel stable and dependable.

logoResearch.name: GE HealthCare
logoResearch.verifiedFact: GE HealthCare is a medical technology company that spun off from General Electric in 2023.
observations: The GE monogram is kept, now in purple instead of the familiar GE blue.
A thin purple wordmark with a capital C in HealthCare marks the new company.

logoResearch.name: Siemens Healthineers
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Siemens Healthineers is the medical technology company of Siemens.
observations: The petrol Siemens wordmark sits above Healthineers in orange.
A cluster of orange dots suggests data, people, or cells coming together.

logoResearch.name: Abbott
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Abbott is a global health care company making diagnostics, devices, and nutrition products.
observations: The symbol is an abstract a, drawn as a rounded box with a line, like a simple medical device.
A bold navy wordmark with tight spacing feels confident.

logoResearch.name: Dexcom
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Dexcom makes continuous glucose monitoring systems for people with diabetes.
observations: A green, wide lowercase wordmark has a playful, approachable look.
The descriptor CONTINUOUS GLUCOSE MONITORING tells you the product in the logo.

logoResearch.name: Philips
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Philips is a Dutch health technology company.
observations: A bold, wide blue wordmark in caps is one of the most stable logos in tech.
Philips also has a shield symbol, but the wordmark is the main logo.

logoResearch.name: Teladoc Health
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Teladoc Health is a virtual care company offering telehealth services.
observations: The open o in Teladoc adds one custom detail to an otherwise heavy wordmark.
Purple and bright blue separate the brand name from the word Health.

logoResearch.name: Zocdoc
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Zocdoc is an online platform for finding and booking doctor appointments.
observations: The yellow symbol is a Z with eyes, a friendly character called Zee.
A heavy dark wordmark keeps the playful symbol grounded.

logoResearch.name: One Medical
logoResearch.verifiedFact: One Medical is a membership-based primary care practice owned by Amazon.
observations: The Amazon wordmark and smile sit next to one medical in teal green.
Lowercase type keeps the brand friendly and close to Amazon's style.

logoResearch.name: Hims & Hers
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Hims & Hers is a telehealth company selling health and wellness products direct to consumers.
observations: The hims wordmark uses a soft serif that feels more like a lifestyle brand than a clinic.
A dark, minimal look makes sensitive products feel discreet.

logoResearch.name: Ro
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Ro is a US direct-to-patient telehealth company.
observations: The two-letter wordmark is one of the shortest names in health care.
Rounded letters in black keep it simple and app-friendly.

logoResearch.name: Headspace
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Headspace is a meditation and mental health app.
observations: A simple orange circle is the symbol, like a calm sun or a blank mind.
The lowercase wordmark is soft and rounded, matching the calm product.

logoResearch.name: Oura
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Oura makes the Oura Ring, a smart ring that tracks sleep and health.
observations: A line above the O looks like a macron and hints at the ring itself.
Thin, wide letters feel premium, like a jewelry or fashion brand.

logoResearch.name: Function Health
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Function Health is a US company offering membership-based lab testing.
observations: The striped orange circle looks like a sun, a body scan, or layers of data.
A light, warm wordmark matches the orange symbol.

logoResearch.name: Hinge Health
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Hinge Health is a digital physical therapy company.
observations: The green symbol is a flexible, looping figure that suggests movement and joints.
A stacked two-line wordmark sits next to the symbol.

listIntro: The boards below show all 45 healthcare logos in one consistent format, grouped into hospitals, insurance, pharma and biotech, pharmacy and medtech, and digital health.
Each logo is reviewed for its design decisions, not for the quality of care or the company's products.
sectionIntroductions: Hospital logos have to work on buildings, signs, and scrubs, so most of them rely on a strong symbol with a clear, institutional wordmark.
Insurers sell trust and stability, so their logos lean on blue, simple shapes, and names that feel safe.
Pharma and biotech brands balance science and humanity, mixing molecules and helixes with friendly scripts and warm colors.
Pharmacies live on storefronts and medtech lives on equipment, so these logos favor bold, legible wordmarks.
Digital health companies compete with consumer apps, not hospitals, and their logos look more like lifestyle brands.
sectionBridge: This is a visual comparison of healthcare logos, not a ranking of hospitals or companies.
Look at how each logo balances trust and warmth, and how much of it is symbol, color, or type.
entryFallbacks: The identity relies on a few clear decisions to stay recognizable.
Notice how the logo would work on a sign, an insurance card, and an app icon.

findings.heading: Real symbols beat generic medical icons
findings.text: Mayo Clinic, Johns Hopkins, and Novo Nordisk use symbols with a story, not stock hearts, crosses, or stethoscopes.

findings.heading: Blue is safe, but other colors stand out
findings.text: Most insurers and medtech brands use blue, while Mount Sinai, CVS Health, and Headspace get noticed with pink, red, and orange.

findings.heading: Pharma is simplifying
findings.text: Pfizer, J&J, Sanofi, and GSK all simplified their logos in the last few years for digital screens.

findings.heading: Digital health looks like consumer tech
findings.text: Hims & Hers, Oura, and Function Health look closer to fashion and lifestyle brands than to hospitals.

logoRosterConfig.checklistHeading: A practical checklist for a new healthcare logo
checklistItems: Does the logo feel trustworthy at first glance?
Does the symbol mean something, or is it a generic medical icon?
Will it work on a sign, a pill bottle, an insurance card, and an app icon?
Is your color different enough from competitors in your category?
Is it simple enough to read at small sizes and in one color?
